extraction.design_notes: 26-week, single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial; participants randomised 2:1 to semaglutide or MDI groups; all analyses performed in the intention-to-treat population.

key_inclusion_criteria: Eligible subjects were adults (age 18–75 years) with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol) on MDI (defined as ≥3 daily injections of insulin analogues, including ≥2 injections of prandial insulin) up to a total daily dose (TDD) of 120 units and ≤0.5 units/kg per day of prandial insulin.
Only metformin and/or SGLT2‐inhibitors were allowed as background diabetes therapy.

evidence.quote: Eligible subjects were adults (age 18–75 years) with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol) on MDI (defined as ≥3 daily injections of insulin analogues, including ≥2 injections of prandial insulin) up to a total daily dose (TDD) of 120 units and ≤0.5 units/kg per day of prandial insulin.

Participants were randomly assigned 2:1 to insulin degludec once daily plus subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once weekly (semaglutide group) or to continue MDI with daily insulin degludec plus prandial insulin aspart (MDI group).
60 individuals were enrolled and randomised to the semaglutide group (n = 40) or the MDI group (n = 20)
Participants randomised to the MDI group were transitioned from their existing basal‐bolus regimen to insulin degludec and insulin aspart.

outcomes.name: Percentage of participants maintaining HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol)

evidence.quote: At Week 26, 36/40 participants (90%) in the semaglutide group and 15/20 (75%) in the MDI group maintained HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol) (odds ratio, 2.6; 95% CI 0.7, 11.0; p = 0.18).
